pattern: Verb Stem + ~아/어 본 적이 있다/없다 (Past Experience 'Have/Haven't done')
meaningEn: Expressing past experience ('have done / have never done').
meaningId: Mengekspresikan pengalaman masa lalu ('pernah / tidak pernah melakukan').

notesEn.usage: Used to state whether one has accumulated experience of doing a specific action in the past.
notesEn.nuance: Use 있다 for 'have done' and 없다 for 'have never done'.

notesId.usage: Digunakan untuk menyatakan apakah seseorang memiliki pengalaman melakukan tindakan tertentu di masa lalu.
notesId.nuance: Gunakan 있다 untuk 'pernah' dan 없다 untuk 'tidak pernah'.

examples.meaningEn: I have been to Korea before.

examples.hangul: 이 영화를 봐 본 적이 있어요?
examples.romaja: i yeong-hwa-reul bwa bon jeog-i is-seo-yo?
examples.meaningEn: Have you ever watched this movie?
examples.meaningId: Apakah kamu pernah menonton film ini?

quiz.question: How do you say 'I have been to Korea' using this structure?
quiz.explanationEn: 가다 transforms into 가 보다 + ~(으)ㄴ 적이 있다 -> 가 본 적이 있어요.
quiz.explanationId: 가다 berubah menjadi 가 보다 + ~(으)ㄴ 적이 있다 -> 가 본 적이 있어요.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: I have been to Korea before. -> 한국에 가 본 ___이 있어요.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: Insert the noun meaning 'experience/time' paired with ~(으)ㄴ.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: Masukan kata benda yang berarti 'pengalaman/waktu' yang dipasangkan dengan ~(으)ㄴ.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'I have been to Korea before.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Saya pernah pergi ke Korea.'
acceptableVariants: 저는 한국에 가 본 적이 있어요
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use Korea to (한국에) + go experience (가 본 적이 있어요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan ke Korea (한국에) + pengalaman pergi (가 본 적이 있어요).

meaningEn: Expressing a decision, plan, or resolution ('decide to do').
meaningId: Mengekspresikan keputusan, rencana, atau janji ('memutuskan untuk').

notesEn.formation: Verb Stem + ~기로 하다 (usually conjugated in past tense ~기로 했어요).
notesEn.usage: States a resolution, decision, or agreement made between people.
notesEn.nuance: Almost always used in past tense because the decision was made prior to speaking.

notesId.formation: Kata Dasar + ~기로 하다 (biasanya dikonjugasikan dalam bentuk lampau ~기로 했어요).
notesId.usage: Menyatakan keputusan, janji, atau kesepakatan yang telah dibuat.
notesId.nuance: Hampir selalu digunakan dalam bentuk lampau karena keputusan telah diambil sebelum berbicara.

examples.meaningEn: I decided to exercise starting tomorrow.
examples.meaningId: Saya memutuskan untuk berolahraga mulai besok.

examples.meaningEn: I agreed to meet a friend on the weekend.
examples.meaningId: Saya berjanji/memutuskan untuk bertemu teman di akhir pekan.

quiz.question: Which structure expresses 'I decided to exercise' using '운동하다'?
quiz.explanationEn: Attach ~기로 했어요 to verb stem 운동하 to state a decision made.
quiz.explanationId: Tempelkan ~기로 했어요 pada kata dasar 운동하 untuk menyatakan keputusan yang telah dibuat.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: I decided to exercise starting tomorrow. -> 내일부터 운동하___ 했어요.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: Attach decision suffix after verb stem 운동하.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: Tempelkan akhiran keputusan setelah kata dasar 운동하.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'I decided to exercise starting tomorrow.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Saya memutuskan untuk berolahraga mulai besok.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use from tomorrow (내일부터) + exercise decision (운동하기로 했어요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan mulai besok (내일부터) + keputusan olahraga (운동하기로 했어요).

pattern: Plain Form + ~고 하다 (Indirect Quotation: Statement 'Says that')
meaningEn: Reporting what someone said ('says that / said that').
meaningId: Melaporkan apa yang dikatakan seseorang ('mengatakan bahwa').

notesEn.formation: Present Verb: ~(ㄴ/느)ㄴ다고 하다 / Adjective: ~다고 하다 / Noun: ~(이)라고 하다 / Past: ~았/했다고 하다.
notesEn.usage: Used to pass on information or statements heard from another person.
notesEn.nuance: In casual speaking, ~고 하다 often contracts to ~대(요).

notesId.formation: Kata Kerja Present: ~(ㄴ/느)ㄴ다고 하다 / Kata Sifat: ~다고 하다 / Kata Benda: ~(이)라고 하다 / Lampau: ~았/했다고 하다.
notesId.usage: Digunakan untuk menyampaikan informasi atau pernyataan yang didengar dari orang lain.
notesId.nuance: Dalam percakapan santai, ~고 하다 sering disingkat menjadi ~대(요).

examples.meaningEn: Minsu says that he is busy tomorrow.
examples.meaningId: Minsu mengatakan bahwa dia sibuk besok.

examples.meaningEn: The teacher said that they are going to Korea.
examples.meaningId: Guru mengatakan bahwa beliau akan pergi ke Korea.

examples.meaningEn: They say that this is Korean food.
examples.meaningId: Mereka mengatakan bahwa ini adalah makanan Korea.

quiz.question: How do you indirectly quote an adjective like '바쁘다' (to be busy)?
quiz.explanationEn: Adjectives take ~다고 하다 directly in present plain form: 바쁘다고 해요.
quiz.explanationId: Kata sifat menggunakan ~다고 하다 secara langsung dalam bentuk plain present: 바쁘다고 해요.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: Minsu says that he is busy tomorrow. -> 민수 씨가 내일 바쁘___ 해요.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: Attach indirect quotation suffix for adjectives.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: Tempelkan akhiran kutipan tidak langsung untuk kata sifat.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'Minsu says that he is busy tomorrow.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Minsu mengatakan bahwa dia sibuk besok.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use Minsu (민수 씨가) + tomorrow (내일) + busy reported (바쁘다고 해요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan Minsu (민수 씨가) + besok (내일) + laporan sibuk (바쁘다고 해요).

pattern: Verb Stem + ~(으)냐고 하다/묻다 (Indirect Quotation: Question 'Asked whether')
meaningEn: Reporting a question that was asked ('asked whether / asked if').

notesEn.formation: Verb Stem + ~(으)냐고 하다/묻다 (or ~냐고 하다 for vowels/adjectives).
notesEn.usage: Used to pass on a question that someone else asked.
notesEn.nuance: In casual spoken Korean, ~냐고 하다 is frequently contracted to ~냬(요).

notesId.formation: Kata Dasar Kata Kerja + ~(으)냐고 하다/묻다 (atau ~냐고 하다 untuk vokal/kata sifat).
notesId.usage: Digunakan untuk menyampaikan kembali pertanyaan yang diajukan orang lain.
notesId.nuance: Dalam bahasa lisan santai, ~냐고 하다 sering disingkat menjadi ~냬(요).

examples.meaningEn: My friend asked where I was going.
examples.meaningId: Teman saya bertanya ke mana saya pergi.

examples.meaningEn: They asked if I was learning Korean.
examples.meaningId: Mereka bertanya apakah saya belajar bahasa Korea.

examples.meaningEn: He asked if I had time.

quiz.question: Which suffix is used to quote a question indirectly?
quiz.explanationEn: ~(으)냐고 하다 is specifically used to relay questions indirectly.
quiz.explanationId: ~(으)냐고 하다 digunakan khusus untuk menyampaikan pertanyaan secara tidak langsung.

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: My friend asked where I was going. -> 친구가 어디에 가___ 물었어요.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: Attach indirect question reporting suffix to verb stem 가.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: Tempelkan akhiran laporan pertanyaan tidak langsung pada kata dasar 가.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'My friend asked where I was going.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Teman saya bertanya ke mana saya pergi.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use friend (친구가) + where to (어디에) + going reported question (가냐고 물었어요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan teman (친구가) + ke mana (어디에) + laporan pertanyaan pergi (가냐고 물었어요).

pattern: Verb Stem + ~(으)라고 하다 / ~자고 하다 (Indirect Quotation: Imperative & Suggestion)
meaningEn: Reporting commands/requests ('told to') and suggestions ('suggested to').
meaningId: Melaporkan perintah/permintaan ('menyuruh untuk') dan usulan ('mengajak untuk').

notesEn.usage: Relays commands (~(으)라고 하다) or suggestions (~자고 하다) made by another person.
notesEn.nuance: For negative commands ('told not to'), use ~지 말라고 하다.

notesId.usage: Menyampaikan kembali perintah (~(으)라고 하다) atau usulan (~자고 하다) dari orang lain.
notesId.nuance: Untuk perintah negatif ('disuruh jangan'), gunakan ~지 말라고 하다.

examples.meaningEn: The teacher told us to do the homework.

examples.hangul: 친구 가 같이 밥을 먹자고 했어요.
examples.meaningEn: My friend suggested that we eat together.

examples.hangul: 의사 선생님이 담배를 피우지 말라고 했어요.
examples.romaja: ui-sa seon-saeng-nim-i dam-bae-reul pi-u-ji mal-ra-go haes-seo-yo.
examples.meaningEn: The doctor told me not to smoke.

quiz.question: Which structure means 'My friend suggested eating together'?
quiz.explanationEn: ~자고 하다 is used to report proposals or suggestions ('Let's...').
quiz.explanationId: ~자고 하다 digunakan untuk melaporkan usulan atau ajakan ('Mari...').

fillInTheBlank.sentenceEn: The teacher told us to do homework. -> 선생님이 숙제를 하___ 했어요.
fillInTheBlank.hintEn: Attach imperative indirect quotation suffix after vowel stem 하.
fillInTheBlank.hintId: Tempelkan akhiran kutipan perintah tidak langsung setelah kata dasar vokal 하.

constructionQuiz.promptEn: Translate to Korean: 'My friend suggested that we eat together.'
constructionQuiz.promptId: Terjemahkan ke bahasa Korea: 'Teman saya mengajak makan bersama.'
constructionQuiz.hintEn: Use friend (친구가) + together (같이) + meal (밥을) + suggested eating (먹자고 했어요).
constructionQuiz.hintId: Gunakan teman (친구가) + bersama (같이) + nasi/makanan (밥을) + ajakan makan (먹자고 했어요).
